episodes.193297: The combination of a digging mid-level trough supported by a shortwave served as the forcing mechanism for thunderstorms across the Upstate of South Carolina. Strong to severe thunderstorms moved into the Northwestern Midlands during the evening hours resulting in areas of wind damage, especially across Newberry and Fairfield counties.
episodes.193313: Gusty showers and thunderstorms across much of Carbon County, Wyoming resulted in reported wind gusts of 60 to 70+ mph on the evening of the 17th.
episodes.193318: Scattered strong to severe storms develop during the late afternoon hours on 8/18. The environment featured a gradient in instability with weaker instability across the western Midlands (mixed layer CAPE around 1000 J/kg) to stronger instability across the central and eastern Midlands (mixed layer CAPE around 2000-2500 J/kg) with sufficient effective bulk shear around 30-35 knots. There was a gradient in moisture with Precipitable water values ranging from 1.5 inches to 1.8 inches in the eastern counties. Some drier air aloft was moving into the area with some downsloping winds at 850/700mb as the upper trough axis approached. The best forcing remained to our north over VA/NC.
episodes.193319: A line of thunderstorms moved south through Middle Tennessee during the evening hours of August 17, 2024. These thunderstorms were severe when they first entered the area with severe winds downing trees and causing minor roof damage. While they weakened below severe criteria as they moved into the Nashville area, winds were still strong enough to down a few more trees.
episodes.193375: A period of northwest flow persisted across Central Alabama for a few days in mid-August, with a ridge over the southwestern United States and an upper low over the Great Lakes. A storm in Cherokee County produced damage on August 16, and storms the next day produced damage across central and eastern counties. On August 18, numerous thunderstorms passed through central and southern counties in Central Alabama, producing widespread tree damage and several instances of hail. A couple areas in Coosa and Tallapoosa counties saw hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.193553: A nearly stationary complex of storms set up over far southwest Connecticut causing record rainfall over 12 inches and devastating flooding. While most of the flooding occurred outside of the county warning area, some flooding did occur in Hartford County.
episodes.193812: A combination of high instability and above average deep layer shear for August with an upper level disturbance resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms. Some storms were severe with damaging wind gusts.
episodes.194246: A few severe storms brough isolated wind damage to portions of the area in the afternoon on 08/18.
episodes.194434: On the periphery of a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) across the western Ozarks, convective outflow helped foster the development of a few thunderstorms across northern Oklahoma. Despite weak wind shear, strong regional instability promoted a few transient severe thunderstorms. A significant downburst event occurred in east-central Garfield County.
episodes.194447: A severe thunderstorm produced golf ball sized hail.
episodes.194448: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.194789: A severe thunderstorm developed over eastern Haakon County during the early morning hours, producing hail to around quarter size in the Ottumwa and Kirley areas.
episodes.194791: Early morning severe storms tracked southeast into Tripp County, producing wind gusts to over 70 mph and hail.
episodes.195106: A series of thunderstorms from a slow moving upper trough brought heavy rain and localized flooding to the Magic Valley.
episodes.195107: The combination of a moisture surge from a large thunderstorm complex over northern Sonora, Mexico and an upper-level trough moving across the Pacific Northwest resulted in the development of thunderstorm activity across south-central AZ during the early morning hours on the 18th. With MLCAPE values near 500 J/KG and DCAPE values of around 1000 J/KG, conditions were favorable for the generation of strong to severe downburst winds.
episodes.195115: A narrow band of elevated thunderstorms developed on the nose of a low-level jet, with around 2000 J/kg MUCAPE and 50 knots of effective shear.  The exposed cell on the south end of the band was the strongest and produced up to quarter size hail.
episodes.195232: A deep area of low pressure centered offshore of Oregon produced moderate to heavy showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.195278: Weak forcing in an unstable atmosphere led to a few instances strong winds.
episodes.195324: A pre-frontal trough and an approaching cold front from upstream thunderstorms combined to spark two areas of storm development that produced severe and damaging wind gusts. The most prolific was a microburst in western Johnston County that shut down Interstate 40 for several hours between North Carolina highway 42 and North Carolina highway 210.
episodes.195368: A few widely scattered thunderstorms produced several gale-force wind gusts over the tidal Potomac River and the Chesapeake Bay from midday through mid evening.
episodes.195386: A couple of isolated severe thunderstorms produced very localized wind damage in King George County, Virginia, and in the western suburbs of Baltimore.
episodes.195387: A couple of isolated severe thunderstorms produced very localized wind damage in King George County, Virginia, and in the western suburbs of Baltimore.
episodes.195415: Scattered showers and storms formed in portions of Western Kentucky during the late afternoon and evening hours with storms remaining sub-severe. Several wind gusts of 40-45 mph were observed at KY Mesonet sites in Muhlenberg, Hopkins, and Todd Counties. In addition to numerous pieces of penny size hail north of Oak Grove, half inch hail in Powderly and dime size hail 6 miles SSE of Cypress in Hickman County were reported.
episodes.195427: Monsoon moisture, an easterly wave, and unseasonable jet stream dynamics fueled scattered thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. One storm produced flash flooding.
episodes.195463: A fairly typical summertime upper level pattern was in place with strong high pressure centered well west of the local area. That put southern Louisiana on the eastern periphery of this ridge in a region of northwestern upper level flow. That setup is often conducive for strong to severe thunderstorm development and what took place on August 17th. Using WPC surface/satellite composite analysis, you can backtrack the convection from an MCS that developed in southeastern Wyoming on the early morning hours of August 16th. In short, it tracked across Nebraska and Kansas on the 16th, through Missouri to Mississippi on the 17th. Daytime heating on the 17th reinvigorated the residual MCS boundary as it moved into the coastal waters.
episodes.195478: High pressure was over Texas in tandem with northwesterly flow on the east side of the high brought a disturbance through Arkansas leading to severe thunderstorms that tracked from northwest to southeast across the state. At the surface, a cold front boundary provided a lifting mechanism for the thunderstorms as the boundary moved from north to south across the state.
episodes.195525: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed southeast across eastern Nebraska and eastern Kansas during the morning and afternoon of the 18th. These thunderstorms weakened before moving into northwestern Arkansas, but additional thunderstorms developed over northwestern Arkansas along the outflow boundary that pushed out from these decaying thunderstorms. The atmosphere over northwestern Arkansas became very unstable during the late afternoon and early evening, which enable some of these storms to produce large hail up to ping pong ball size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195538: With above normal moisture in place across eastern Utah and western Colorado, and passing shortwaves adding some extra lift and instability, round after round of daily showers and thunderstorms had already been ongoing for 2-3 days prior to August 18th. This meant that, by the afternoon of the 18th, the atmospheric profile was fully saturated, meaning any stronger shower or storm could produce heavy rainfall and high rainfall rates. In addition, there was some indication that training of storms would be possible during the afternoon hours, heightening the risk for heavy rain, flash flooding, and debris flows.
episodes.195597: Waves of showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced widespread showers and thunderstorms. A few storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts, knocking down trees and power lines across portions of eastern Pennsylvania.
episodes.195598: Waves of showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced widespread showers and thunderstorms. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts, knocking down trees and power lines across portions of New Jersey.
episodes.195720: Deep moisture combined with an approaching cold front and a favorable position of the jet stream triggered numerous heavy rain producing thunderstorms over Central New York. Locally heavy rainfall totaled between 3 and 4 inches over a short period of time which caused areas of flooding.
episodes.195721: Deep moisture combined with an approaching cold front and a favorable position of the jet stream triggered numerous heavy rain producing thunderstorms over northeastern Pennsylvania. Locally heavy rainfall totaled between 3 and 4 inches over a short period of time which caused areas of significant flash flooding.
episodes.195779: A coastal low pressure system led to prolonged periods of heavy rainfall in northwest Connecticut on August 18, 2024. Rainfall totals were greatest in southern Litchfield County where total accumulations ranged from 1.75 to 8.80. As a result, numerous instances of flash flooding were reported. Flash flooding led to numerous road closures, damaged roadways, and damaged business parking lots. Additionally, numerous home basements became flooded. The towns most impacted included Oxford, Roxbury, and Woodbury. The extent of flooding and damaged sustained thereafter, led to President Biden approving Connecticut Governor, Ned Lamont's request for Federal Emergency Declaration which included Litchfield County.
episodes.195786: On Sunday August 18th, a cold front was stretched from northwest Kansas...southeastward into south central Kansas. As the day wore on, this boundary would become the focal area for several areas of showers and thunderstorms developing. With increased instability by the late afternoon, a thunderstorm developed in Barber county, eventually producing severe criterion hailstones near Medicine Lodge, KS.
episodes.195791: A strong south-southwesterly upper-level low triggered a round of severe thunderstorms and strong outflow winds along the east slopes of the Cascades, extending into eastern Oregon. Numerous reports of damaging wind gusts and small hail were reported.
episodes.195793: A strong south-southwesterly upper-level low triggered a round of severe thunderstorms and strong outflow winds along the east slopes of the Cascades, Reports of severe hail were received from the public.
episodes.195822: A strong upper level low pressure system was in place across the Great Lakes region heading into the morning hours of Saturday, August 17. From this a cold front draped southwestward, moving towards the state throughout the day. By the time it reached western Kentucky during the afternoon hours. the warm/unstable airmass ahead of the boundary had already spawned showers and thunderstorms. A line of storms formed ahead of the front and continued to outpace the frontal passage eastward. By the time it reached eastern Kentucky, multiple severe thunderstorm warnings were issued for these strong storms. Throughout the afternoon and evening hours, widespread wind damage occurred in numerous counties. Multiple locations also saw damaging hail.  While the main line of storms fizzled out during the evening hours in the far east, additional discrete thunderstorms continued ahead and all the frontal boundary into the overnight for central and eastern Kentucky.
episodes.195851: A mature upper low with an embedded shortwave allowed for a couple rounds of scattered severe thunderstorms to cross East Tennessee, with hail and damaging thunderstorm winds occurring.
episodes.195854: Isolated thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts and marginally large hail.
episodes.195855: Widely scattered thunderstorms and isolated storm clusters moved across upstate South Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. A few of the storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195862: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina throughout the afternoon into the early evening. Several of the storms produced severe weather in the form of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195869: An isolated thunderstorm moved into Cherokee County late in the afternoon. The storm briefly became severe in the Gaffney area.
episodes.195893: A late evening severe thunderstorm in Tucson resulted in wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.195900: A line of thunderstorms moved across North and Central GA through the afternoon and evening hours of the 7th. Generally storm motion was not conducive to tap into shear energy, however a few storms which moved more eastwardly were able to tap into both the instability and shear. The greatest storm damage was reported in Hall and Coweta County where extended swaths of wind damage were noted. Some hail up to ping pong ball sized was also reported in northeast GA, early on in the event.
episodes.195901: A remnant cold pool from an MCS in the Central Mississippi Valley was able to tap into afternoon summertime instability on the evening of the 18th. Thunderstorms were scattered in nature but relatively long lived with stretches of wind damage originating from individual cells all the way from the Atlanta Metro down past Macon.
episodes.195920: In advance of an approaching cold front, showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon. One of these storms reached severe levels and produced damaging winds which downed two trees.
episodes.195971: Thunderstorms moved across southwest Alabama and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.196020: Thunderstorms developed over portions of central South Dakota during the overnight hours of August 18th. This activity became severe and tracked southeast into portions of north central Nebraska during the early morning hours of August 18th. Thunderstorm wind damage was reported in Holt county along with quarter sized hail in Boyd county.
episodes.196086: An MCS developed across central Virginia on August 17, producing heavy rain and flash flooding as it slowly moved east.
episodes.196087: A cold front approached Virginia from the west on August 18. Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of the front, producing large hail, damaging winds, and localized flash flooding.
episodes.196097: Thunderstorms brought severe outflow wind gusts.
episodes.196102: Had another in a period of severe weather days.
episodes.196103: A cold front approached Virginia from the west on August 18. Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of the front across Virginia before moving over the Chesapeake Bay. These storms produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.196107: A cold front approached Virginia from the west on August 18. Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of the front, producing large hail, damaging winds, and localized flash flooding.
episodes.196116: Thunderstorms brought gusty winds to much of Utah and flash flooding to southern Utah.
episodes.196154: Gusty winds associated with a thunderstorm caused a tree to fall onto power lines.
episodes.196195: A frontal system over the area on August 18th allowed for the development of rain early in the morning. As the day progressed, mesoscale features including multiple boundary interactions and a mesolow allowed thunderstorms to continue to intensify with persistent back-building and training over the same areas in southern Connecticut. These thunderstorms produced anywhere from 3-4.5 inch per hour rainfall rates resulting in several considerable Flash Flood Warnings and a Flash Flood Emergency being issued. Numerous rescues, road and bridge washouts, and several mudslides resulted in widespread damage. Several large-stem rivers including the Naugatuck, Pomperaug, Housatonic, and Still Rivers all reached major flood stage at some point during the day as a result of a widespread 5-8 inches of rainfall with localized amounts of up to 12-13 inches. Unfortunately, 3 people lost their lives in Connecticut as a result of the flash flooding.||Preliminary damage assessment costs for Fairfield County is $5.8 million and New Haven County is $4 million. This is not a final number.
episodes.196196: A frontal system over the area on August 18th produced heavy thunderstorms that were fairly slow moving over northeast New Jersey. A cold front moving in from the west late in the afternoon produced heavy thunderstorms with an environmental MUCAPE of 2000-3000 J/kg and PWAT values of 1.7-1.8 inches. These slow moving thunderstorms produce rainfall rates of 1-3 inches per hour over New Jersey with total rainfall amounts of 2-4 inches. This resulted in widespread flash flooding during the evening of August 18th.
episodes.196215: An upper level trough approached aloft as a cold front approached at the surface. Clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed west of the area. Given 0-6 km Bulk Shear and MLCAPE values around 1000 J/kg, one storm became severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.196217: An upper level trough approached aloft as a cold front approached at the surface. Clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed west of the area. Given 0-6 km Bulk Shear and MLCAPE values around 1000 J/kg, some storms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.196256: One thunderstorm became severe across southern Herkimer County during the afternoon hours on August 18, 2024 downing trees and wires.
episodes.196285: As a surface low moved east across the Great Lakes, its trailing cold front dropped south through the Midwest and towards the Lower Ohio Valley. Multiple rounds of convection worked through central Kentucky. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging winds, resulting in scattered damage across central Kentucky.
episodes.196318: A line of severe thunderstorms moved southward across Mississippi during the evening of August 18th and produced scattered to widespread wind damage.
episodes.198689: An occluded surface low drifted eastward from southern Lake Huron toward western Lake Ontario during the early morning through early afternoon of the 18th as the trailing cold front swept southeastward across Lake Erie, northeast OH, and northwest PA. Scattered rain showers accompanied the front as it encountered sufficient moisture and weak MUCAPE over Lake Erie. The updraft of one of these showers spawned a non-mesocyclonic waterspout offshore Cuyahoga and Lake Counties in northeast OH.
episodes.198941: At the surface, a low wobbled southeastward from the northwestern Great Lakes to southern Lake Huron during the early evening of the 16th through early evening of the 17th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from northern Lake Michigan and central Lake Erie to near the northern shore of Lake Ontario and Upper St. Lawrence River Valley, while the trailing cold front moved eastward from the Upper Mississippi River Valley to central Lake Erie and north-central OH.||Within the warm and moist sector, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms persisted eastward along the shore of far-northeast OH and generated a gale-force peak convective wind gust at Conneaut Breakwater Light during the early evening of the 16th. These storms occurred in an environment with weak MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear. During the early afternoon through early evening of the 17th, additional multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted northeastward or eastward over and near the southern shore of Lake Erie, along and ahead of the cold front. These storms generated isolated gale-force peak convective wind gusts amidst moderate MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.
